name: CA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Bera holds an overwhelming cash advantage: $1.65M on hand vs $27K for Tucker
District leans Democratic (D+6) with a favorable national environment for the party
Prediction markets price Bera's win probability at roughly 95-96%
No public polls or expert ratings available, limiting independent confirmation
model.rationale: The district's six-point Democratic lean, an environment favoring the party, and Bera's roughly 60-to-1 cash-on-hand edge over Tucker all point to a comfortable incumbent win, and prediction markets at 95-96% agree. With no polls or expert ratings signaling any competitive dynamic, there is no basis to move materially away from these fundamentals.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Bera or a sharply nationalized electorate could tighten the race more than current indicators suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ami Bera, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Sacramento-area district that leans Democratic by six points. He enters the general election with a commanding financial edge, holding about $1.65 million in cash after raising $1.4 million, while Republican Robb Tucker has roughly $27,000 available. Neither outside groups nor independent polls have played a measurable role in the contest so far.

Prediction markets put Bera's chances at roughly 95 percent, and the district's fundamentals point the same direction. With a well-funded incumbent, a lightly funded challenger, and no visible signs of a competitive dynamic, the seat sits firmly in the Democratic column heading into November, though the absence of polling leaves some room for surprise.
